pillars.heading: Why funPaste
pillars.lede: Many clipboard managers turn everything you copy into one long list. funPaste keeps recent text, images, files, favorites, and prompts together in one keyboard-first panel.

items.title: Stay in flow
items.body: Press Shift+Command+V from any app, move with the arrow keys, and press Enter to paste back where you were working.

items.title: Prompts are first-class
items.body: Save reusable prompts and complete {{feature}} and {{constraints}} before pasting.

items.title: Local-first
items.body: No account, telemetry, ads, or network sync. Your history, prompts, and favorites stay on your Mac.

simulation.heading: Try the panel
simulation.lede: This is a browser simulation of the panel, not the live app. Switch categories, search, and select items with the keyboard. Enter selects an item in the simulation — it does not paste into another application.

features.heading: What it does
features.lede: funPaste works more like a deck of content cards than one long clipboard list.
items: Records text, image, and file clipboard history; duplicates move to the top.
Search recent clips with fast keyboard navigation.
Create, edit, and delete your own prompts and favorites.
Favorite recently copied text or images in one click.
Complete prompt variables before copying or pasting.
Pause recording or clear all history at any time.
Runs as a menu bar agent without taking space in the Dock.
Automatically uses an English or Simplified Chinese interface.

install.heading: Install in a few steps
install.lede: The current beta is ad-hoc signed and not notarized by Apple, so the first launch needs one extra step.

steps.title: Download the universal DMG
steps.body: One build covers Apple silicon and Intel Macs on macOS 14 or later.

steps.title: Drag funPaste to Applications
steps.body: Open the DMG and drag the app into your Applications folder.

steps.title: Control-click and choose Open
steps.body: On first launch, Control-click the app and choose Open, then confirm. macOS will warn that the app is not notarized.

steps.title: Allow Accessibility (optional)
steps.body: Allow funPaste in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility. This is used only to simulate Command+V. Without it, copying and manual paste still work.

privacy.heading: Privacy is not a footnote
privacy.lede: funPaste can access what you copy, so its privacy boundaries are explicit.
points: The app makes no network requests and does not write clipboard contents to logs.
Clipboard history and the content library are persisted through macOS UserDefaults without additional app-level encryption.
Sensitive-content filtering is heuristic and cannot identify every password, token, or piece of personal information.
Accessibility permission is used only to simulate Command+V; without it you can still copy and paste manually.

download.heading: Copy with one shortcut

help.title: Setup guide
help.intro: This guide covers installing funPaste, handling the first-launch warning, granting the Accessibility permission, and making your first paste.

sections.body:
1. Download the latest universal DMG from the Releases page.
  2. Open the DMG and drag funPaste into Applications.
  3. The DMG covers Apple silicon and Intel Macs running macOS 14 or later.

Because the beta is ad-hoc signed and not notarized by Apple, macOS will warn on first launch:

  1. In Applications, Control-click funPaste and choose Open.
  2. Confirm that you want to open it. The warning appears because the app is not notarized, not because a problem was detected.
  3. After the first confirmation, funPaste opens normally on later launches.

funPaste requests the Accessibility permission only to simulate Command+V and paste the selected item back into the app you were using.

If you deny the permission, clipboard recording and copying still work — you just paste manually with Command+V.
  1. Open System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility.
  2. Enable funPaste in the list.
  3. If the panel still cannot paste automatically, quit and reopen funPaste.

1. Copy something in any app.
  2. Press Shift+Command+V to open the panel.
  3. Use ↑ / ↓ to move the selection.
  4. Press Enter to paste the selected item where your cursor was.
  5. Press Esc to close the panel without pasting.

• The panel does not open: confirm funPaste is running (menu bar icon), and that no other app has claimed Shift+Command+V.
  • Automatic paste does not work: re-check the Accessibility permission, or paste manually with Command+V.
  • The app was moved or deleted: re-copy from Applications; macOS preferences may persist after uninstall and can be removed in System Settings.
